node.title: Exact physical relative-continuant orientation reduction
node.statement: Fix finite R>1, n>=2, either relay sign sigma=+1 (max) or sigma=-1 (min), and an arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete transverse common-terminal root with m=2n events. For the relative log(q) Jacobi recurrence let alpha_i=-sigma a_i with a_i>0 and define the symmetric (m-1)-by-(m-1) path matrix by (L_sigma)_(ii)=1/a_i+1/a_(i+1)-sigma K_i and (L_sigma)_(i,i+1)=-1/a_(i+1). Its terminal flux satisfies w_m=sigma(product_i a_i)det(L_sigma)=-q sigma(R-1)J, and partial_q A_n=(q^2-1)w_m/(q p^2 r^2). Therefore J<0 iff det(L_sigma)>0 iff sign(partial_q A_n)=sigma. Moreover det(L_sigma)=0 iff the distinguished q-Jacobi field has both terminal position components zero. These statements are made in the relative quotient by the ever-present scaling field; they neither assert det(L_sigma)>0 nor identify positive definiteness of L_sigma with the required determinant orientation.

node.title: Orient the final physical relay continuant
node.statement: Prove det(L_sigma)>0 for every premise-complete physical relay word, thereby signing the exact R6 causal functional J, or rigorously certify a physical word with nonpositive determinant and the additional global witness needed for an O3a refutation.
node.formal_statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, sigma in {+1,-1}, and every premise-complete transverse common-terminal relay root, prove that the final determinant of the physical relative path matrix L_sigma is positive. Then separately upgrade the local q-twist to global fixed-mu root order across all chambers and compatible closures. Alternatively certify a premise-complete physical root with det(L_sigma)<=0 and all bifurcation, distinctness, terminal, phase, indexing, norm, and relay predicates required to refute universal O3a.
discharge_criteria: Cover every finite R>1, every n>=2, both signs, every premise-complete transverse chamber, and compatible closures.

Positive definiteness, positivity of every leading continuant, and the full complementary-inertia theorem are stronger sufficient statements, not equivalent reformulations of the required final determinant sign.
Alternating coefficient signs, local phase bounds, local diagonal inequalities, palindromy, or the coefficient-only n=2 saturated word do not establish the physical determinant orientation.
Finite binary64 scans and positive sampled pivots are non-propagating evidence and cannot prove the universal statement.
A local determinant or twist sign must still be upgraded to global one-root order before reflection can imply uniqueness.

node.title: Physical continuant, spectral inertia, and finite-contrast singularity continuation
node.statement: Combine exact physical event gluing, the relative Dirichlet path operator, Schur-complement inertia, time-translation forcing, and a preregistered finite-contrast singularity search to refine the R6 causal-resolvent frontier. The exact continuant reduction is proved, but the universal determinant sign and global root order remain open.

falsification_tests: Quotient out the permanent scaling field before interpreting a path-matrix kernel.
Do not replace the final determinant orientation by the stronger positive-definiteness or full-inertia conjecture.
Do not promote an abstract alternating coefficient word to a physical relay without common-energy and all-cell momentum gluing.
Do not infer a universal phase order from reflection-fixed samples or use the failed M-matrix supersolution candidate.
Do not promote a finite null search or sampled positive pivots to a proof.

ordered_steps: For zeta=q partial_q z, use the zero signed pairing with the scaling field to define the equal cell Wronskian w and the relative event value d; exact saltation gives w_i-w_(i-1)=alpha_i d_i with alpha_i=-sigma a_i and a_i>0.
Use the exact two-frequency cell DtN formula and the all-cell phase bound to obtain d_(i+1)-d_i=K_i w_i with every K_i finite and nonzero.
Eliminate d_i to obtain the symmetric Dirichlet path operator L_sigma on relative fluxes, explicitly quotienting the permanent scaling field which maps to d=w=0.

Use the log(q) initial data w_0=0, d_1=-1, w_1=sigma a_1 and the last-row source L_sigma W=(w_m/a_m)e_last; a corner cofactor or continuant induction gives w_m=sigma(product a_i)det(L_sigma), including at singularity.
Apply the accepted terminal symplectic and causal identities to get w_m=-q sigma(R-1)J and partial_q A_n=(q^2-1)w_m/(q p^2 r^2).

Because q, R-1, every a_i, p^2, and r^2 are positive in scope, conclude J<0 iff det(L_sigma)>0 iff sign(partial_q A_n)=sigma; keep positivity of the determinant as an open obligation and positive definiteness as a stronger sufficient conjecture.
boundary_cases: Covers max and min separately, n=2 and all n>=2, every finite R>1, both endpoint cells, and asymmetric as well as reflection-fixed transverse common-terminal roots.
The relative coordinates quotient the permanent scaling field; no claim is made about all nonzero physical Dirichlet fields.
The determinant-zero terminal equivalence concerns only the distinguished q-Jacobi line and simple nonzero terminal derivatives.
Grazing events, switch collisions, unfinished relay IVPs, and closures where the accepted simple-root formulas cease to be defined require a separate limiting theorem.
No finite computation, sampled phase order, full-inertia conjecture, or abstract coefficient word enters the proof.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: The exact R7 reduction makes det(L_sigma)>0 equivalent to the still-open finite-contrast sign J<0. Neither physical phase ordering, a determinant sign theorem, nor a premise-complete nonpositive physical determinant has been established.

The route proves a new exact continuant representation and corrects a scaling-quotient scope error, but its stronger Hardy/inertia candidates remain open, its natural supersolution was numerically falsified, and the formal finite search found no certifiable counterexample.
